However `lang/pt_BR.json:804` translates the verification subject with the button wording.

conventions.evidence: `app/Http/Controllers/PasswordResetController.php:54-64` validates three fields with a multi-rule password set inline instead of the Form Request the conventions ask for beyond one or two fields; no test files exist anywhere in `change.diff` although every feature must ship with a test. Positives: `CHANGELOG.md:26` updated, PHPDoc on public methods (`PasswordResetController.php:16-29,41-43,49-51`), escaping with `{{ }}`, no service layer.

security.evidence: `PasswordResetController.php:32-34` validates the e-mail, `:54-64` validates token/e-mail/password (min 8, letters, mixed case, numbers, confirmed); `routes/web.php:656-658` throttles password.email and `:667-669` protects verification with auth+signed+throttle; both forms carry `@csrf` (`forgot-password.blade.php:265`, `reset-password.blade.php:302`); all output uses `{{ }}`; `VerifyEmailController.php:17-22` aborts 403 unless id and hash match; no enumeration leak because the same `passwords.sent` flash is always returned (`PasswordResetController.php:36-38`).

tests.evidence: No Pest/PHPUnit test file appears anywhere in `change.diff`; the only test-adjacent edit is the `phpunit.xml:22-24` locale pinning, so none of the new routes, controllers, translations or mail theme are covered.

simplicity.evidence: Mostly lean and reuse-first (framework `Password` broker, stock `ResetPassword`/`VerifyEmail` notifications, default route naming), but `PasswordResetController.php:57-62` repeats `min:8` both as a string rule and in `PasswordRule::min(8)`, and both auth views duplicate the same document skeleton (`forgot-password.blade.php:249-255`, `reset-password.blade.php:286-292`).

readability.evidence: Small single-purpose methods with PHPDoc (`PasswordResetController.php:16-29,41-43,49-51`), intention-revealing names (`store`, `edit`, `update`), clear named routes (`routes/web.php:653-668`), consistent formatting, no dead code or debug output.

scope.evidence: Every touched file serves the task: `.env.example`, `phpunit.xml`, `config/mail.php`, theme CSS, the two auth views, `lang/pt_BR.json`, `routes/web.php`, the two controllers, `User` implementing `MustVerifyEmail` (`app/Models/User.php:177`) and the `CHANGELOG.md:26` entry; nothing from the out-of-scope list (no login/registration, Livewire, layouts, SCSS/JS).

issues.explanation: The change ships no Pest/PHPUnit tests at all, leaving the reset flow, verification endpoint, mail rendering and pt-BR strings unverified and violating the mandatory test-first convention.

The contract treats "Verify your email address" as a notification subject, but it is translated as the button copy "Verifique o endereço de e-mail"; requirement 3 expects the subject "Verifique seu endereço de e-mail".
The update action validates three fields with a multi-rule password set inline, whereas the project uses a Form Request once rules grow beyond one or two fields.
The hash comparison uses `!==` rather than `hash_equals()`; this is not exploitable with a publicly derivable verification hash, but constant-time comparison is the Laravel house pattern.
`min:8` is declared twice (string rule plus `PasswordRule::min(8)->letters()->mixedCase()->numbers()`), so one declaration is redundant.

review.summary: The change delivers the pt-BR password-reset and e-mail-verification endpoints with Laravel's stock notifications, a pegafila markdown theme using the #0f7490 brand button, the required locale pins, routes and translation keys. It ships no tests at all, which the project's test-first rule makes mandatory, and it maps the verification subject to the button wording, so the verification mail subject is wrong. The rest of the code is clean, secure and in scope, but these points need fixing before merging.
